title: Ordered log synchronizer with trace-sampling horizon
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: implement an ordered-log synchronizer service that reduces false-negative trace joins caused by out-of-order arrival from edge collectors, while bounding added ingestion latency via a configurable 'trace-sampling horizon'. The synchronizer will sit between edge/proxy collectors and the existing Loki/ELK ingestion cluster, performing lightweight buffering, per-tenant ordering windows, and conditional trace-aware sampling before forwarding. This aims to improve trace->log correlation accuracy for latency/error dashboards without unbounded buffering costs.

Scope in: ordered buffering per tenant and trace-id prefix, horizon-driven release, backpressure signals to collectors, metrics and dashboards for window hits/misses, integration with Loki ingestion path and ES pipeline.

Out of scope: rewriting downstream indices, long-term cold reordering, cross-tenant global coordination, complex heuristics for root cause analysis (left for future work).

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Key constraints: memory budget per tenant, SLO for 95th percentile added latency <= 150ms at steady state, fail-open to passthrough on heavy pressure, deterministic behavior across restarts for in-flight windows (use persisted minimal watermark), and observability hooks for tracing and sampling decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Ordered synchronizer accepts incoming structured log batches and emits them in trace-consistent order within the configured horizon
When arrival exceeds horizon, synchronizer emits immediately and increments 'horizon_expired' metric
End-to-end added p95 latency from collector to Loki <= 150ms under normal load (measured in perf harness)
Service exposes per-tenant memory usage, window counts, backpressure events, horizon hits/misses, and sampling decisions to Console
Graceful degrade: if synchronizer overloaded, it toggles to passthrough within 30s and alerts on Console
comments: 2026-02-11 - Ava Martinez: Kickoff notes. Discussed per-tenant windows (default 120ms) and a customer-facing knob 'trace_sampling_horizon_ms'. Agreed to start with in-memory ring buffer + persistent minimal watermark in RocksDB for restart safety.

2026-02-18 - Ravi Patel: POC completed for single-tenant flow. Local harness shows 40% reduction in missed trace links for skewed edge arrival. Github PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/834

2026-02-25 - Priya Shah (SRE): Reviewed backpressure behavior. Requested explicit circuit breaker metric and an operator toggle in Console. Raised concern: memory amplification with large trace fanout; recommended tenant soft-limit and approximate LRU eviction policy.
2026-03-02 - Design review (Ben Cho): UX for Console - add 'horizon' heatmap and per-route breakdown. PM (Olivia Reed) approved rollout plan with 1% canary for high-volume customers first.

2026-03-08 - Ravi Patel: Benchmarks on m10 cluster: p95 added latency 120ms at 5000 rps, memory per-tenant within budget. Found pathological workload where a single trace emits 50k tiny messages; added protection: max-entries-per-trace cap and aggregate forwarding for high-fanout traces.
2026-03-10 - Security review request submitted by Ravi: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SCR-1296
implementation_plan: 1) Prototype in telemetry service as feature-flagged component (POC done)
2) Add persistent minimal watermark store and eviction policy
3) Wire metrics to Console and create horizon heatmap dashboard
4) Run perf harness and tune defaults; implement max-entries-per-trace guard
5) Canary rollout: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> all tenants, with kill-switch and monitoring alerts
6) Post-deployment: 2-week monitoring window and SLA verification
risks_and_mitigation: Buffer blowup for high-fanout traces: mitigate with cap+aggregate-forward and tenant soft-limits
Increased ingest latency impacting SLOs: keep conservative default horizon (100-150ms), measure in perf harness, and provide per-route override
State loss on crash: persist only minimal watermark and keep windows reconstructable from recent sequence tokens
Operator confusion: expose simple controls in Console and document expected trade-offs in design doc
